speaker: Doctor
text: The lack of reversibility on the bronchodilator test makes asthma less likely, pointing towards COPD or another chronic obstructive process. Given your age and the spirometry results, do you have any history of smoking or significant occupational exposure to irritants? I would also like to request a CT scan of the chest to look for emphysema or bronchiectasis. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal CT scan rules out significant structural lung disease like emphysema or bronchiectasis, which is unusual for typical COPD. Given the recent upper respiratory infection and persistent obstruction without reversibility, I need to check for other causes. Do you have any history of heart failure, or do you experience swelling in your legs and fatigue? REQUEST TEST: BNP_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Since cardiac causes and structural lung diseases are ruled out, I suspect a condition like ABPA or eosinophilic bronchitis. Do you have a history of allergies or nasal polyps, and have you noticed any blood-tinged sputum? REQUEST TEST: Total_IgE_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal IgE and CT findings, I am now considering post-infectious airway hyperreactivity or eosinophilic bronchitis. Have you noticed any improvement in your symptoms with the use of inhaled corticosteroids, and do you have a history of nasal polyps or chronic sinusitis? REQUEST TEST: Eosinophil_Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal IgE and eosinophil counts, allergic and eosinophilic causes are unlikely, so I am considering a viral-induced persistent cough or cough-variant asthma. Have you tried using inhaled corticosteroids for any duration, and did you experience any relief from your symptoms? REQUEST TEST: Methacholine_Challenge_Test

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the persistent obstructive pattern with a normal methacholine challenge, which effectively rules out asthma, and the recent history of an upper respiratory infection, this presentation is most consistent with post-infectious cough with reactive airway disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Post-infectious Cough
